# On-Call Readiness Checklist

"The reminder" below is the weekly pre-shift Slack post in your rotation's channel, generated by the [oncall-prep skill](../../.agents/skills/oncall-prep/SKILL.md) from live Datadog and Slack data. A shorter handoff post follows on Wednesday after 13:00 ET with your status and last week's incidents.

## 1. Schedule

- [ ] Confirm your name is on the shift in [Datadog Schedules](https://us5.datadoghq.com/on-call/schedules).
- [ ] If you need coverage, record the replacement in Datadog as an override so pages reach the right person.

Done when: the schedule shows you for the full shift window and the reminder reports no escalation gaps for your rotation. If the reminder reports a gap, reply in your rotation’s reminder thread.

## 2. Datadog can reach you

Set in [your Datadog profile](https://us5.datadoghq.com/personal-settings/profile?tab=on-call-notifications).

- [ ] Install the Datadog mobile app, sign in to the us5 org, and allow notifications. Guide: [Configure your mobile device](https://docs.datadoghq.com/incident_response/on-call/guides/configure-mobile-device-for-on-call/?tab=ios).
- [ ] Save the Datadog Contact Card on your phone and set it to Emergency Bypass (iOS) or a Do Not Disturb exception (Android). Guide: [Telephony channels](https://docs.datadoghq.com/incident_response/on-call/guides/configure-mobile-device-for-on-call/?tab=ios#telephony-channels-voice-calls-and-sms).
- [ ] Add and verify your phone number in your Datadog profile. Guide: [Contact methods](https://docs.datadoghq.com/incident_response/on-call/notification_preferences/#contact-methods).
- [ ] Enable push, SMS, and voice for high-urgency alerts. Configure two channels to notify you immediately and the third within five minutes. Guide: [Notification preferences](https://docs.datadoghq.com/incident_response/on-call/notification_preferences/#notification-preferences).
- [ ] Enable push for low-urgency alerts.
- [ ] Join `#alerts-p1-critical` and `#alerts-p2-high-impact` in Slack. Every monitor that pages posts there too, so the thread is where the alert context, the auto-triage, and teammates land. The reminder flags this as `not in #alerts-p1-critical` / `not in #alerts-p2-high-impact`.
- [ ] With Do Not Disturb on, open [your Datadog On-Call profile](https://us5.datadoghq.com/personal-settings/profile?tab=on-call-notifications). Under **Contact methods**, hover over your phone number and use **Test Call** and **Test SMS**; hover over your mobile device for its test option. Confirm the call rings and the SMS and push notifications arrive. Guide: [Test contact methods](https://docs.datadoghq.com/incident_response/on-call/notification_preferences/#contact-methods).

Done when: the reminder shows a green circle after both :datadog: and :slack: next to your name (it checks the Datadog side and the two alert channels only) and the contact-method tests above reach your phone with Do Not Disturb on. These tests check contact methods, not notification-rule timing or escalation-route coverage.

Note: a live call dials your verified phone number directly and skips you if there is none.

## 3. Access

Before your shift, confirm you can sign in to each service below.

- [ ] [Datadog](https://us5.datadoghq.com/account/login/id/7dc1ecb4-8653-11ee-b24f-da7ad0900005?saml_config_uuid=d877cb08-b6e2-4e60-8ccb-bdc19741f18d)
- [ ] [Status page notices](https://us5.datadoghq.com/status-pages/3bdfe680-d6e4-4a0b-9c04-c25058c342e0/notices): the **New notice** button is enabled. If not, ask a Datadog admin to add you to the **Engineers** role (it carries `status_pages_incident_write`; the Standard role does not). The reminder flags this as `cannot publish status page notices`.
- [ ] [On-Call pages](https://us5.datadoghq.com/on-call/pages): you can acknowledge a page and [declare an incident](https://us5.datadoghq.com/incidents) without a "assign yourself a seat" prompt. If you hit one, ask a Datadog admin for a role that carries `on_call_respond` and `incident_write` (Engineers or Standard). The reminder flags this as `cannot acknowledge pages` / `cannot manage incidents`.
- [ ] [Devin](https://openrouter.devinenterprise.com/)
- [ ] [GitHub](https://github.com/OpenRouterTeam/openrouter-web)
- [ ] [Pylon](https://app.usepylon.com/support/issues/views/inbox)
- [ ] [Cloudflare](https://dash.cloudflare.com/)
- [ ] [Vercel](https://vercel.com/openrouter)
- [ ] [GCP](https://console.cloud.google.com/welcome?project=openrouter-core)
- [ ] [Infisical](https://app.infisical.com/organizations/97292866-f6eb-449c-9e63-a2aa4c3457dc/projects)
- [ ] [Clerk Protect rules](https://dashboard.clerk.com/apps/app_2PXGbmOMh7zKN2sZcuDqtuwZsOX/instances/ins_2PiQqkvRQeepwGvkV1YD8Aot5zR/protect/labs) (rules that challenge or block sign-in and sign-up)
- [ ] [Oncall PAM Google Group](https://groups.google.com/a/openrouter.ai/g/on-call/members)

Done when: every login works without a password reset or approval.

## 4. Reading

- [ ] Read [Priority and Severity](./severity.md): severity levels, paging rules, and when to post a status-page notice.
- [ ] Review [Paging](./paging.md): which rotation gets paged and how escalation works.
- [ ] Read [First 15 minutes](./first-15-minutes.md): your role’s actions after a page.
- [ ] Read [During an incident](./during-incident.md) and [After an incident](./after-incident.md): mitigation, customer updates, closure, and follow-up.

Done when: you can choose the severity, know who to page, and find your role’s next steps.

## 5. Handoff

- [ ] Ask the outgoing on-caller what is open: muted monitors, ongoing incidents, flaky alerts, deploys planned for your week.
- [ ] Skim the postmortems linked in the Wednesday handoff post and reply there once done.
- [ ] First handoff of the month (Engineering Primary): call the live line +1 315-889-4536, press 2, and confirm it rings you. Note the result in the handoff thread.

Done when: you know what could page you this week before it does.
